title: Choose the visual world for JARVIS
question: Fresh hand. The roll assigned Dot Matrix. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Dot Matrix
options.lineage: Minimal dot-matrix device interfaces and LED glyph lights
options.thesis: JARVIS as one calm black device: white dot-matrix readouts, plain sentences, and a single red light that only means 'look here'.
materials: a glyph light ring for voice
options.viewport: Home is a black face: a ring of light (JARVIS's voice state) beside one big dot-matrix status line, then three plain rows for what to do next.
options.risk: Can feel sparse or cold if the plain-language sentences are too short to explain anything.

raised.raise: Every status sentence is followed immediately by the evidence that proves it (source, value, time).
A changed reading stays lit until you have seen it, instead of silently updating.
The thing you are working on burns brightest; everything else steps back to grey.

options.label: Vital Signs
options.thesis: Your PC's vitals as monitor channels: each one a colour, a live trace and a big number, calm until an alarm tier is reached.
options.viewport: Home shows CPU, memory, disk and network as four monitor channels with traces and big numbers; alerts sit in a bar above.
options.risk: Close to the dark-screen-with-glowing-lines look most 'futuristic dashboard' runs end up with.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.lineage: Factory Records sleeves (pulse-line plot on matte black)
options.thesis: A stack of thin white pulse lines on matte black draws your PC's activity; everything is a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: Home is one large pulse-line plot of recent activity with a small catalog index of screens.
options.case: Very futuristic and striking; loses on 'easy to understand' because colour codes replace words.
options.risk: Beautiful but cryptic: users must decode labels.

options.label: Split-flap Board
options.thesis: Scans, findings and actions as rows on a departure board that flip when their status changes.
options.viewport: Diagnostics as a board: each check is a row with status flaps (OK, DELAYED, FAILED).
options.case: Great for scan progress and status lists; weaker for chat and voice.

options.label: Monochrome Product Page
options.thesis: One neutral scale, one rare accent, every claim paired with proof.
options.viewport: Claims and proof screenshots in alternating rows.
options.case: A marketing page, not an app you operate.
options.kept: Every claim followed by its proof.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.thesis: Subsystems as coloured lines meeting at interchanges.
options.viewport: Your PC drawn as a metro map.
options.case: A PC is not a journey; the metaphor costs clarity.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: Airline boarding passes and gate boards
options.thesis: Ranked rows that rerank in place; changes stay lit.
options.case: Too close to the transit world you already re-rolled away from.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain colours below, a purple course above.
options.viewport: A course of checks drawn over a terrain of your PC.
options.case: Light, outdoorsy and specialist; not futuristic or simple.
options.kept: A fixed base layer that the active task never edits.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Windows 11 style dashboard: sidebar, cards and a blue accent, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar on the left, a grid of health cards on Home, charts on Monitor.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every system utility and gaming-laptop app.
